answer.justification: The recurrent laryngeal nerve supplies nearly all intrinsic laryngeal muscles; unilateral injury after thyroidectomy causes vocal cord palsy and persistent hoarseness. The nerve is intimately related to the inferior thyroid artery's branches, so ligation near the poles/endangers it. Internal laryngeal nerve injury causes sensory loss; external laryngeal nerve injury mainly weakens high-pitched voice; edema would be transient and generally resolves within two weeks.
